712598.t: From Proto-Indo-European *seǵʰ- (“to hold”) + -δον (-don, adverbial suffix); related to ἔχω (ékhō, “to hold”) and σχῆμα (skhêmă, “form; shape”).

712545.t: From Proto-Indo-European *súHs (“swine”); doublet of ὗς (hûs). The reason for the survival of initial /s/ in this form is unknown.

712560.t: From συνίστημι (sŭnĭ́stēmĭ, “to place together, associate, unite”) + -μα (-mă).

712589.t: The formation is similar to δάκτυλος (dáktulos) and κόνδυλος (kóndulos), probably first from a noun *σφόνδος (*sphóndos).

712597.t: Unknown. Traditionally believed to be a substantivization of the adjective σχέδιος (skhédios, “near, close”).

712567.t: Beekes marks the word's origin as unknown.

712505.t: From συντάσσω (suntássō, “to put together”) + -μα (-ma) and συν- (sun-) + τάγμα (tágma, “command, order”)

712576.t: σφάλλω (sphắllō, “to fall, to be cast down”) + -μα (-mă, suffix forming neuter nouns)

712575.t: From Proto-Indo-European *(s)gʷʰh₂el- (“to stumble”). Compare Old Armenian սխալեմ (sxalem, “to err”), Sanskrit स्खलति (skhalati, “to stumble”) and possibly Latin fallō.

712583.t: Generally considered to be from Proto-Indo-European *bʰey- (“bee”). Beekes rejects this in favor of a Pre-Greek origin possibly shared with ψήν (psḗn, “gall-insect”).

712543.t: From a zero-grade of Proto-Indo-European *twer- (“to twirl, swirl”); see the related σαίρω (saírō, “to sweep”) for cognates.

712515.t: συντέμνω (suntémnō, “to cut down, cut short”) + -ος (-os), in the o-grade.

712586.t: Adverbial neuter accusative plural of σφοδρός (sphodrós).

712578.t: Often connected with σφεδανός (sphedanós), σφοδρός (sphodrós), σφαδᾴζω (sphadāízō), and Sanskrit स्पन्दते (spandate, “to vibrate, tremble, quake”), as well as with Latin funda (“sling”), with formation structure similar to that of ἀγχόνη (ankhónē), βελόνη…

712587.t: Clearly related to σφεδανός (sphedanós, “violent, vehement”). The origin of these words is uncertain but perhaps related to σφαδᾴζω (sphadāízō, “to flounce”) and σφενδόνη (sphendónē, “sling”).

712581.t: Unknown. Has been linked to Sanskrit स्फ्य (sphyá, “oar; spar”) and Proto-Germanic *spēnuz (“chip; shaving”), but this is phonologically impossible due to the aspirated labial /pʰ/ in Greek.

712591.t: Formation similar to κληΐς (klēī̈́s) and κνημίς (knēmī́s) which points to a secondary derivative.

712592.t: Julius Pokorny connects this word with σπαίρω (spaírō, “to hammer, to make rapid movements”).

712558.t: From συν- (sun-, “with, together”) + στέλλω (stéllō, “to dispatch, to send”).

712585.t: According to Beekes, perhaps of Pre-Greek origin, apparently based on the pre-nasalization of the -γγ- (-ng-) as well as the lack of credible cognates in other Indo-European branches.

712571.t: Of unknown origin, with no known cognates outside Greek. Furnée connects φάσγανον (phásganon, “sword”) as φασγ-/σφαγ-, suggesting a Pre-Greek origin.

712551.t: From συν- (sŭn-) + σκότος (skótos, “darkness”) + -άζω (-ắzō); the unprefixed verb σκοτάζω (skotắzō) is attested later.

712527.t: From συν- (sun-, “with”) + τυγχάνω (tunkhánō, “to happen (to), I succeed, I light upon, I obtain”).

712595.t: Probably from a Proto-Indo-European *skeh₂- (“to split”), and generally compared with Sanskrit छ्यति (chyati, “to split, hurt”), from the root छो (cho, “to cut off”).
